proof.text: First prove that the presheaf unit is locally surjective, by TensorProduct.induction_on applied to the property that its image sieve is covering. For zero, every restriction has preimage zero, so the image sieve contains the top sieve. For r ⊗ m, the image sieve of r under q is covering by the hypothesis hq. If f belongs to that sieve, choose a coefficient lift a with q(a)=res(r). The section a • res(m) maps to q(a) ⊗ res(m) = res(r) ⊗ res(m), by linearity of the unit and TensorProduct balancing. The pure-tensor restriction formula identifies the latter tensor with res(r ⊗ m). Thus the image sieve of r ⊗ m contains this covering sieve. For a sum x+y, intersect the covering image sieves given by induction. Along an arrow of the intersection, add its two preimages; additivity gives a preimage of res(x+y). GrothendieckTopology.intersection_covering and superset_covering conclude the induction. This includes zero tensors, zero modules, zero rings and empty coverings.

proof.text: On underlying abelian presheaves the second factor of the specified unit is definitionally CategoryTheory.toSheafify J (changeOfRingsPresheaf q F).presheaf. Mathlib supplies local surjectivity directly as (J.W_toSheafify _).isLocallySurjective, using the WEqualsLocallyBijective assumption already in the statement. Compose this with the locally surjective presheaf unit using Presheaf.isLocallySurjective_comp. The resulting local surjectivity is also Sheaf.IsLocallySurjective for the image of the unit under SheafOfModules.toSheaf. Mathlib Sheaf.epi_of_isLocallySurjective makes that image epic, and the faithful functor toSheaf reflects epimorphisms via epi_of_epi_map. These are the two required conclusions.

title: tensor quotient epimorphism
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site, small in a universe containing the coefficients [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Let $q:R'\to R$ be a morphism of sheaves of commutative rings that is locally surjective: every section of $R$ lifts to $R'$ after a covering of its domain. Let $F$ be a sheaf of $R'$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Form the sheaf tensor product $R\otimes_{R'}F$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and regard it as an $R'$-module via $q$. Then the canonical $R'$-linear map
$$F\longrightarrow R\otimes_{R'}F,\qquad m\longmapsto1\otimes m,$$
is locally surjective and is an epimorphism of sheaves of $R'$-modules.
